hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, a single carbon joined to four completely different groups.
Start with 3-methylhexane, CH3CH2CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3, and list the four groups on the branched carbon.
Now test the symmetrical molecule CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH(CH3)2 for any carbon with four different groups and see what you find.
walkthrough:
**Recall the chiral centre test**

A chiral centre is a tetrahedral carbon with four different atoms or groups attached. For alkanes, look for a CH carbon with H plus three different alkyl groups.

Rule:
$$\text{chiral C} = \text{C attached to 4 different groups}$$

**Check the common molecule 3-methylhexane**

CH3CH2CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3 has a branch at C-3. That carbon is joined to H, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

All four are different, so this molecule is chiral.

**Check 2,3-disubstituted pentanes**

CH3CH(CH3)CH(CH3)CH2CH3 and CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH(CH3)2 both contain a CH carbon joined to H, methyl, ethyl and isopropyl-type groups. That gives one chiral centre in each molecule.

**Spot the molecule without a chiral centre**

CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH(CH3)2 is 2,4-dimethylpentane. The two CH carbons each carry two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, and the $\text{CH}_2$ carries two H atoms.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$
No carbon has four different groups, so it is achiral. Only the pair containing this molecule qualifies.

options.A: Both are chiral. The first is 3-methylhexane with a chiral C-3 bonded to H, methyl, ethyl and propyl. The second is 2,3-dimethylpentane with a chiral C-3 bonded to H, methyl, ethyl and isopropyl.
options.B: Both are the same hydrocarbon, 3-methylhexane, written two ways. CH(CH2CH3)CH3 is identical to CH(CH3)CH2CH3. The branched carbon has four different groups, so both are chiral.
options.C: Both are chiral. The first is 3-methylhexane as above. The second is 2,3-dimethylpentane, CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH(CH3)2, whose C-3 is bonded to H, methyl, ethyl and isopropyl, so it is chiral.
options.D: This pair qualifies. The first, CH3CH(CH2CH3)CH(CH3)CH3, has a chiral centre. The second, CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH(CH3)2, is 2,4-dimethylpentane and is symmetrical with no carbon bonded to four different groups, so it has no chiral centre.
